claim: The Potential Fraud Detection module renders its six pages from the national radar export: the radar with real 2024 figures, the Kentucky psychoeducation blow-up and case file, the reallocation what-if, tools and data coverage, and the backtest.
assertions: Radar header: the lede reads $54.0B to 1,269 flagged services in 2024 with $46.7B above what enrollment predicts, mostly a billing convention; the money bar splits it by tier with "Worth review: $3.7B · HIGH $212.2M (11) + VERIFY $3.5B (74)" and "Likely convention: $40.2B (599)"; the 51-tile map colors Kentucky by $396M worth review with a HIGH dot, and the Kentucky panel shows HIGH 1 and VERIFY 3. The first ranked row is Kentucky psychoeducation (H2027), $143.0M, 78.3% of US, suggested HIGH.
Radar header: switching the map to all dollars above the line shows New York at about $12.6B.
Radar: at 1600px the score and suggested-tier column fits inside the table without horizontal scrolling.
Radar: clicking the Florida tile shows the Florida panel and filters the list to 24 Florida rows.
Radar: clicking the selected state again clears the state filter.

Program blow-up: opens on Kentucky psychoeducation with Kentucky selected on a 51-tile state map and H2027 (HIGH) first in the program list; the chart has a four-swatch legend, share of US 78.3% and about 44× the fair share on top, and the caption reads $143.0M paid against a $3.2M fair share.
Program blow-up: clicking the 2023 bar switches the page to Kentucky psychoeducation 2023.
Program blow-up: clicking the Ohio tile lists Ohio's 7 programs that blew up in 2024, and one click opens another program.
Program blow-up: 0 states with no blow-up in any screen year are disabled on the map.
Case file: Kentucky psychoeducation 2024 shows 7 fired and 8 pending signals, the explanation review, and the referral panel opens from "Refer to the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit".
Case file: the module grows with its content and the app footer follows it (no overlap).

Reallocation: Kentucky at 60% upheld frees $438.5M of $730.8M above the enrollment line ($314.7M federal); switching to the General Fund flags over-allocation, and "fit to available" rescales the needs to the $123.7M state share.
Tools and data coverage: 24 analyses with running, ready or needs-data status, the data sources with load dates, and the last scan console.
Backtests: all 7 known cases pass (5 flagged, 2 conventions not flagged).
